root_cause.text: The security descriptor buffer in build_sec_desc() was allocated with kmalloc() instead of kzalloc(), leaving the reserved field (Sbz2) uninitialized and causing protocol-compliant Samba servers to reject it when non-zero slab garbage is present.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "When building an ACL descriptor in build_sec_desc(), we are using a kmalloc()'ed descriptor buffer... This never writes to the 2 byte reserved field, leaving it as uninitialized heap data." The patch changes `kmalloc(nsecdesclen, GFP_KERNEL)` to `kzalloc(nsecdesclen, GFP_KERNEL)` to zero-initialize the entire buffer.
